correctness.rationale: The two-forced-image contraction lemma is proved by decomposing its directed functional graph into closed cycles and exactly n-2 open paths, whose random completion is a uniform permutation of the paths. Summation gives E[K B_H] with every degree and two-cycle boundary term, and subtracting E[K]=h_n and E[B_H]=2e/n yields (c+2e/n-d_1-d_n)/n(n-1). Exact graphwise enumeration (all H through n=5), 280 conditioned image cases and both sign-opposed star labelings agree; finite tests are explicitly not the universal proof. n=2 and complete/empty graphs are covered.

Mansour–Shattuck Introduction, Theorems 2.3, 2.4 and Section 3 jointly count disjoint cycles and *cycle successions*, namely arrows j to j+d within the cycle representation, not edges between consecutive one-line values.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Although the source's marginal adjacency statistic is the path specialization and the other source's joint cycle statistic is stronger in a different direction, neither source covers the same joint pair. In fact the directed cycle-succession count Q=sum_{j<n}1{Pi(j)=j+1} has covariance -(n-1)/n^2 with K, whereas the one-line undirected path statistic has positive covariance (n-2)(n+1)/(n^2(n-1)) for n>=3. Thus a cycle-succession formula is not an equivalent joint law for B_H, and the arbitrary-graph endpoint-degree sign classification is not implied by the inspected marginal laws.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2008 random-genome common-adjacency paper provides marginal adjacency laws, the 2009 adjacent-pair paper provides marginal equidistributions, the 2013 unseparated-pair paper gives a marginal bijection, and the 2016 cycle-succession paper studies arrows within disjoint cycles rather than consecutive one-line values. None of the inspected statements is a mixed covariance with the same permutation's disjoint-cycle count, nor an arbitrary-graph endpoint-degree/sign law. The finite all-graph identity and the sign reversal under relabeling abstract stars are the claimed contribution; implicit historical mixed-moment coverage remains a risk.
residual_risks: A classical bivariate Eulerian/Stirling or general two-image permutation-pattern generating function may contain the covariance implicitly, even though the inspected titles and theorem statements do not state the arbitrary-graph endpoint-degree formula.
Marginal equidistribution results must not be treated as evidence for joint novelty without preserving the cycle-count coordinate.
Database discovery coverage is finite, and partitions do not establish global originality or uniqueness.

value.rationale: The exact all-graph result collapses a pair of natural permutation observables—disjoint cycles/Cayley distance and preserved allowed adjacent values/genome breakpoint similarity—to only graph edge count, overlap with a reference path, and two endpoint degrees. It determines the covariance sign for every allowed-pair constraint; moreover the identical abstract star is negatively correlated when centered at an endpoint yet positively correlated at an interior vertex for all n>=3. This is a structural labeling-sensitivity classification beyond marginal adjacency enumerations and not an arbitrary chosen finite slice.
